correctness.rationale: For each η>0, the stopped reflected Brownian–OU generator gives the unique first two hitting-time moments. The derivative with respect to weak propulsion amplitude reduces exactly to two Dirichlet–Neumann scalar resolvents. The passive moment factorization has a simple interior root; applying the implicit-function theorem gives the stated coefficient. Explicit polynomial inverses give χ(0+)=4/125. Direct hyperbolic resolvent asymptotics give χ(η)=-1/η+O(η^-2) at infinity. The standalone checker verifies the endpoint symbolically, compares independent Green quadratures to the elementary formula, and obtains matching finite-amplitude derivatives from a truncated independent Hermite PDE discretization. The truncation is corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating article contains a full analytical treatment for Gaussian velocity initialization but treats fixed initial/reset velocities numerically (Sec. 3.4) and does not give the signed zero-amplitude susceptibility or the rigorous slow/fast persistence reversal. The general first-passage restart criterion from 2017 does not imply a model-specific OU response coefficient without solving coupled moment equations. The 2021 boundary perturbation article gives a technique, not the present reset-onset formula. Claim-directed search of published mathematical records and available existing claims identified no exact covering statement. This is provisional originality rather than a proof of priority.
residual_risks: General perturbation or spectral resolvent treatments not retrieved could imply the all-persistence formula as a specialization.
The 2021 weak-activity boundary paper was checked only at abstract/metadata level; a full-text implicit derivation was not excluded.

The motivating numerical fixed-velocity simulations use normalized OU reset speeds of ±1, matching the prescribed normalized velocity here; their finite-amplitude plots could contain implicit information about sign changes, although they do not print the analytic susceptibility or its exact asymptotic coefficients.
The sign-crossing is proven to exist but uniqueness is neither claimed nor established.

value.rationale: The paper’s numerical study flags reset propulsion orientation as a major determinant of resetting efficiency but does not resolve its weak-amplitude analytical dependence on persistence. The sign-reversal theorem gives a falsifiable, natural transport-phase prediction across a continuous physical relaxation parameter, with two exact coefficients and an exact all-rate response formula. It distinguishes a genuinely persistent outward bias from a short-lived one, rather than optimizing an arbitrarily chosen small parameter or recomputing a known table.
